State machines

Source: vignettes/state-machines.Rmd
state-machines.Rmd
library(simcompR)

The state_machine block is a finite state machine inspired by Stateflow charts. It is a discrete block: it runs at the sample hits of its clock and holds its outputs in between.

Semantics

At every sample hit the block:

  1. collects the transitions leaving the active state, sorted by priority (smaller first) and then by their position in the list;
  2. fires the first one whose guard is true and whose after time (time spent in the active state) has elapsed;
  3. runs, in order, the exit action of the old state, the transition action and the entry action of the new state, and records the entry time;
  4. if no transition fires, runs the during action of the active state.

At most one transition fires per hit, so evaluation always terminates, and the ordering never depends on R list iteration details. Outputs are computed after the transition: the outputs at a hit reflect the inputs at that hit.

Guards and actions are strings (portable, checked against a whitelist) or R functions. Guards see u (the input vector), t, elapsed and the data variables; actions assign data variables.

A timed traffic light 

m <- sim_model("traffic")
sim_add_block(m, "constant", "enable", value = 1)
sim_add_block(m, "state_machine", "light", period = 1,
  states = c("red", "green", "yellow"),
  transitions = list(
    sim_transition("red", "green", after = 3),
    sim_transition("green", "yellow", after = 2),
    sim_transition("yellow", "red", after = 1)),
  outputs = list(red = 1, green = 2, yellow = 3))
sim_connect(m, "enable", "light")
r <- sim_run(sim_compile(m), c(0, 12), times = 0:12)
data.frame(t = sim_times(r), state = c("red", "green", "yellow")[sim_signal(r, "light.state")])
#>     t  state
#> 1   0    red
#> 2   1    red
#> 3   2    red
#> 4   3  green
#> 5   4  green
#> 6   5 yellow
#> 7   6    red
#> 8   7    red
#> 9   8    red
#> 10  9  green
#> 11 10  green
#> 12 11 yellow
#> 13 12    red

The output ports are state (the index of the active state), y (the per-state outputs, when given) and data (when there are data variables).

Guards, priorities and data

A counter of how many times the machine re-entered state a:

m <- sim_model("counter")
sim_add_block(m, "time", "t")
sim_add_block(m, "state_machine", "sm", period = 1,
  states = c("a", "b"),
  transitions = list(
    sim_transition("a", "b", "u[1] >= 2", action = "n <- n + 10"),
    sim_transition("b", "a", "TRUE")),
  entry = list(a = "n <- n + 1"),
  data = c(n = 0))
sim_connect(m, "t", "sm")
r <- sim_run(sim_compile(m), c(0, 6), times = 0:6)
cbind(t = sim_times(r), state = sim_signal(r, "sm.state"), n = sim_signal(r, "sm.data"))
#>      t state  n
#> [1,] 0     1  1
#> [2,] 1     1  1
#> [3,] 2     2 11
#> [4,] 3     1 12
#> [5,] 4     2 22
#> [6,] 5     1 23
#> [7,] 6     2 33

The entry action of the initial state runs once, at the first hit, with the inputs and time of that hit, before any transition is tried.

A thermostat in closed loop

A heater controlled by a two-state machine with hysteresis. The room cools toward 10 degrees and the heater adds 2 degrees per unit time.

th <- sim_model("thermostat")
sim_add_block(th, "integrator", "temp", initial = 18)
sim_add_block(th, "state_machine", "ctrl", period = 0.1,
  states = c("heating", "idle"),
  transitions = list(
    sim_transition("heating", "idle", "u[1] > 21"),
    sim_transition("idle", "heating", "u[1] < 19")),
  outputs = list(heating = 1, idle = 0))
sim_add_block(th, "mux", "mx")
sim_add_block(th, "expression", "rate", expr = "2 * u[1] - 0.1 * (u[2] - 10)")
sim_connect(th, "temp", "ctrl")
sim_connect(th, "ctrl", "mx", output = "y", input = 1)
sim_connect(th, "temp", "mx", input = 2)
sim_connect(th, "mx", "rate")
sim_connect(th, "rate", "temp")
r <- sim_run(sim_compile(th), c(0, 30))
plot(r, c("temp", "ctrl.y"))

The machine samples every 0.1 time units, so the temperature overshoots the thresholds slightly; this is the expected behavior of a sampled controller.

Static checks

sim_check_state_machine() reports unreachable states (ignoring guards) and states without outgoing transitions, and errors on unknown states or ambiguous priorities. The block runs the structural checks when it is built.

sim_check_state_machine(c("off", "on", "fault"),
  list(sim_transition("off", "on", "u[1] > 0"),
       sim_transition("on", "off", "u[1] <= 0")),
  initial = "off")
#> $unreachable
#> [1] "fault"
#> 
#> $absorbing
#> [1] "fault"
sim_check_state_machine(c("a", "b"),
  list(sim_transition("a", "b", priority = 1),
       sim_transition("a", "a", priority = 1)))
#> Error:
#> ! State 'a' has transitions with the same priority; the order would be ambiguous.

Formal verification of state machine properties (for example with the sibling package ‘z3r’) is planned, not part of this release.
